messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Performance/SLO recap & MAP items

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the performance and SLO-related items we discussed and the proposed next steps (MAP = mutual action plan).

SLO checklist (as discussed):
- Latency targets: p95 generation <= 300ms (for short-form responses ~<128 tokens); p99 streaming latency <= 500ms end-to-end
- Throughput: sustain ~1200 tokens/sec overall for peak workloads (we measured ~1k tokens/sec in the demo)
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent active users (avg 6–8 requests/sec per user during spikes)
- Streaming: server-sent chunking with max buffer latency 100ms; client reassembly acceptable
- Cold-start: acceptable first-token latency budget = 800ms; warm starts should be under p95 target above
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model (quantized) if capacity constrained; configurable degrade-to-latency policy

Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist.pdf, demo-recording.mp4 (linked below).

Proposed MAP / next steps:
1) We run a 30–60 minute performance evaluation using your sample prompt set (we provide instructions + telemetry collection).
2) Redwood provides a canary config (batching + concurrency + streaming flags) and recommended reserved capacity for the trial window.
3) We share a short SOW/quote and trial contract to lock in reserved capacity for the benchmark.
4) Meet (30 min) to review perf-run results and confirm decision criteria for GA.

Can you confirm the decision criteria you want us to measure in the perf run (e.g., p95 latency, p99 streaming latency, token/s sustained for 15m window, error rate under 0.1%)? Also let us know the sample prompt set size (approx number of unique prompts and typical input length).

I'll loop in Vivek (solutions) and Laura (AE support) to prepare the perf-run plan once you confirm.

Best,

Thanks, Aditya — great summary. A few clarifications from our side before we kick off the perf run: 

- Streaming SLA: our users are latency-sensitive when composing trades — we need p99 streaming latency <= 450–500ms end-to-end (from user keystroke to final token in UI). Is that achievable with your streaming pipeline or do you recommend different tuning?
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent users is the right peak number to plan for. Typical active requests during market hours are bursts of 5–10 requests per user, each ~80–200 tokens.
- Cold-start budget: 800ms is reasonable, but please provide an example cold-start profile (first-token p50/p95) for the model variant you recommend.
- Throughput: we care about sustained tokens/sec over 15m windows; aim for no more than 10% degradation during sustained periods compared to short bursts.
- Data retention / logs: we will need audit logs for requests (30 days) and evidence for SOC2 controls — can you confirm Redwood can provide those?

Decision criteria for us: if perf run meets p95 <=300ms and streaming p99 <=500ms with error rate <0.1% over a 30-minute sustained period, we move to a 60-day trial (reserved capacity) and evaluate cost.

We'll provide a 500-line sample prompt set (mix of short and mid-length prompts) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director of Product, FinTechCo
Samantha.Lee@fintechco.com

Thanks for the context, Aditya. Quick plan below — high level config + MAP items we should present to the customer.

Proposed perf-run config (30–60m sustained run):
- Model: open-variant-2.1 (quantized int8) — balance of latency and quality for FinTechCo prompts
- Infra: 2x dedicated g5.8xlarge-like GPUs (reserved for the 30–60m window) to avoid noisy neighbors
- Batching: dynamic batching with max_batch_size=64, target latency p95=~250–300ms for <=128-token responses
- Concurrency: allocate capacity for 220 concurrent connections (buffer for spikes); use request token limit 512
- Streaming: enable chunked streaming with client buffer target 50–100ms; measure end-to-end p99 streaming latency
- Cold-start profile: cold-first-token p50 ~400ms, p95 ~780ms (on reserved infra) — we'll measure during the run

MAP / deliverables:
1) Perf run orchestration + telemetry collection (we provide a script; customer supplies sample prompt set and a simple traffic driver).
2) Post-run report: p50/p95/p99 latencies, sustained tokens/sec over 15m windows, error rate, tail latency distribution, and recommended canary configs.
3) Cost estimate for reserved capacity (hourly + 60-day reserved option) and SOW draft.
4) SOC2 evidence: we can provide request logs (30 days), access logs, and architecture description; for audited evidence we coordinate with security to provide redacted samples.

I'll draft the perf-run orchestration and share the run command + telemetry schema by EOD. Attaching perf-run-instructions.md.

Next suggested step: schedule the perf run on Mon 16 Jun @ 10am PT (confirm if that works for the FinTechCo team).
